summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands on embedded software experience across STM32, NVIDIA Jetson, and Arduino platforms. Built real time firmware in bare metal C and FreeRTOS, including interrupt driven sensor integration and multi servo actuator control over UART, I2C, and SPI.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture recognition glove, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth over serial interfaces to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and embedded integration end-to-end.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) on a Cortex-M4 target; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on STM32, integrating VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling from a Jetson-based YOLOv8 detector.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection for closed-loop grasping.
Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer; resolved 11 integration failures to achieve 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
